summary: In a fiction excerpt from Book 15, Ray hands out mysterious rings to Rodriguez and Kilgore, saying they are for protection. Kilgore jokes about them and Rodriguez fixates on the inscription 'For the terror that comes by night.' Ray, burdened by unanswered questions and his memories of men lost in Ba'dai, refuses to explain and tells Rodriguez to ask him tomorrow. He worries about Ziggy and Nina, who likely know he has gone missing, and about Emma, and he reflects on the unfairness of withholding knowledge from his men. The passage ends abruptly in a tense scuffle in the kitchen.
one_line: Ray hands out mysterious protective rings to Rodriguez and Kilgore, withholding explanations while burdened by losses and loose ends.
key_facts: Ray tells Rodriguez and Kilgore to each pick a ring and put it on, saying the rings are for protection.
Kilgore says the rings are more interesting than a unit patch.
Rodriguez traces the inscription on his ring and reads aloud, 'For the terror that comes by night.'
Kilgore responds that the inscription is 'a little weird.'
Ray flashes back to Ba'dai, where Whitfield and the others collapsed like discarded garments, puddles of vacated flesh.
Ray considers that Holcomb may have learned a lesson or two in the desert, but still wants to punch him in the skull.
Ray tells Rodriguez, 'Ask me tomorrow, Rodriguez,' which he recognizes as a surrender of sorts.
Ray worries that Ziggy thinks he has gone AWOL and that Nina, who has heard rumors of murders in the sub-decks, is probably out of her mind with worry.
Ray wonders whether being an officer all the time is what it is like and whether it is too late to turn down his commission.
Rodriguez creates a thundershower of crockery in the kitchen after springing away from Kilgore.
